newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares closed higher on Thursday, boosted at the outset by Wall Street's 93 point gain on Wednesday and further buoyed by gains in Dutch bonds.

But dealers said trading had been thin throughout the session as the market remained uncertain about the trend of U.S. interest rates after recent economic data. "We've had conflicting data out of the U.S. (recently) and nobody really wants to take a view on interest rates," one dealer said.
The AEX index closed 10.05 points or 1.38 percent higher at 739.63. "Not so long ago I'd have said that was a significant move, but it seems to be normal nowadays," a dealer said.

Dealers said the recent spin downwards in financial markets after stronger than anticipated March U.S. PPI figures and subsequent pick-up after milder than expected U.S. CPI data had fostered confusion and hestitancy in Amsterdam.
"We're very unsure in terms of what's going to happen with interest rates," a dealer said. "The market's very nervous."

Dealers said the Amsterdam market appeared to be awaiting Friday's options expirations with little anxiety. "I think the game has been played on the derivatives markets, most of the positions have been sorted out," said a dealer. Options-related business was said to be behind some of Wednesday's decline.

Dealers said 740 on the AEX was forming up as strong short term resistance ahead of Friday's expirations. "We saw selling come out whenever the index got up to 740," one dealer said, adding he believed it was because because some players had index options expiring around that level and were selling the cash market to defend their positions.
"Volume has been so low today it's been quite easy to pressurise some prices," he added.
Gains among the leaders ranged to 7.00 guilders, as in Unilever at 363.00, while Philips put on 2.30 guilders to 90.80 and Royal Dutch rose 4.70 guilders to 335.40.

Photocopier maker Oce van der Grinten closed 4.80 guilders down at 223.00 after an initial 3.50 guilder gain evaporated. The shares bounced initially after yesterday's 11.50 guilder drubbing triggered by first quarter figures on Tuesday.

Television producer Endemol dropped 2.80 guilders to 49.90 after a newspaper report the firm faces tough renewal terms in its talks with RTL TV of Germany, which could cut the value of its existing three year contract, due to expire soon.
The company said it had just started negotiations and the story was premature. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
